title: Qualify a Rust class-group mathematical core
objective: Implement the Rust class-group core qualification plan through complete native and browser evidence, preserving Sage.js public semantics, proof authority, portability, and measured PARI comparisons

oracles: Independent exact relation, ideal, transformation, generator, and completion certificates
Existing Sage.js dynamic class-group and class-unit contracts
exceptions: This campaign evaluates attributed handwritten Rust mathematical algorithms as an explicit, receipt-gated architecture exception rather than source-transparent lowering of an ordinary Python body.

handoff.summary: R0/W0 foundations and R1--R3 cubic work now include strict contracts, pinned PARI controls, validated arbitrary-precision prepared inputs, complete GRH-conditional relation/class-map/unit/regulator evidence for the open cubic panel, a fail-closed Sage.js qualification-receipt adapter, and exact full-row-6 execution in Node, Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through a qualification-only GMP/MPFR/FLINT Wasm reactor. These remain qualification components rather than a production class-group backend.
risks: The complete Rust prepared-field engine has not yet been integrated behind the Sage.js public result types or lifecycle API.

The complete browser path currently uses a synchronous qualification route rather than the Sage.js Web Worker product API and lacks cancellation, retained map handles, lifecycle qualification, and competitive Firefox performance.

The certified preparation and receipt adapters currently cover cubic conditional-GRH requests only; the first blind held-out cubic campaign completed 3 of 12 cases, and the untouched confirmation set must remain unexecuted until general fixes are ready.
next_steps: Finish the balanced private 60-open plus 60-held-out corpus without committing held-out answers.
Define and implement the Rust reactor/result ABI so the complete prepared-field result becomes an ordinary Sage.js class-group object without JSON phase round trips.

Integrate the complete class-and-unit reactor through the actual Sage.js Web Worker route, then qualify cancellation, lifecycle, retained maps, cold start, and browser performance before broader-degree expansion.
